rationale: The literature confirms that MMDS1 (NFU1), MMDS2 (BOLA3), and related early-stage MMDS types typically present with infantile-onset leukoencephalopathy, lactic acidosis, hyperglycinemia, and specific vascular/cardiac hallmarks like early pulmonary arterial hypertension (MMDS1) or dilated cardiomyopathy (MMDS2). In contrast, FDXR-related MMDS9B predominantly manifests as a progressive sensorial neuropathy characterized by optic atrophy, sensorineural hearing loss, movement disorders, and ataxia, typically lacking early fatal pulmonary hypertension, marked nonketotic hyperglycinemia, and cystic leukodystrophy.

evidence.text: MMDS1 due to NFU1 mutations presents with lactic acidosis, hyperglycinemia, epileptic encephalopathy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which serve as key hallmarks of classic iron-sulfur cluster assembly defects.

source.title: A Case of Multiple Mitochondrial Dysfunctions Syndrome 1 and Review of the Literature
source.quote: Identification of the clinical combination of lactic acidosis, PAH, and hyperglycinemia during diagnostic evaluation should raise suspicion for a defect of the ISC pathway

evidence.text: MMDS types 1 to 5 manifest with early-onset severe leukoencephalopathy, with diagnostic suspicion raised by elevated lactate, pyruvate, and glycine in body fluids, alongside specific signs like pulmonary hypertension (MMDS1) or dilated cardiomyopathy (MMDS2).

source.title: A Review of Multiple Mitochondrial Dysfunction Syndromes
source.quote: Despite certain specific clinical elements such as pulmonary hypertension or dilated cardiomyopathy in MMDS type 1 or 2, respectively, nearly all of the patients with MMDS presented with severe and early onset leukoencephalopathy. Diagnosis could be suggested by high lactate, pyruvate, and glycine levels in body fluids.

evidence.text: FDXR-associated disease manifests clinically with optic atrophy, sensorineural hearing loss, movement disorder, and neurological dysfunction rather than the classic infantile fatal leukoencephalopathy with pulmonary hypertension seen in MMDS1.

source.title: Ferroptosis is a novel pathogenic mechanism of FDXR-related mitochondriopathy
source.quote: Clinically, FDXR-related mitochondriopathy is characterized by optic atrophy, neurological dysfunction, movement disorder, hearing loss

evidence.text: FDXR mutations manifest predominantly with sensorial neuropathies, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of mitochondrial iron-sulfur protein disorders beyond classic severe early MMDS phenotypes.

evidence.text: An early cohort study identified 14 patients from 13 families surviving well beyond early infancy (aged 1.6 to 20 years) presenting with FDXR-associated multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: To what degree do CSF and plasma glycine and lactate levels remain strictly normal across different age groups in FDXR-mutant individuals?
new_directions.rationale: MMDS1-3 systematically show marked elevations in glycine and lactate due to combined lipoate-dependent enzyme deficiencies; verifying whether MMDS9B patients consistently show normal glycine is crucial for using nonketotic hyperglycinemia as an absolute negative discriminator.

new_directions.question_text: What is the incidence of subclinical or late-onset white matter cystic cavitation on high-resolution neuroimaging in MMDS9B compared to IBA57/MMDS3?
new_directions.rationale: Differentiating whether cavitation is completely absent or merely delayed in FDXR patients will determine whether normal white matter morphology on early MRI definitively rules out MMDS1-3 in favor of MMDS9B.
